title: Suthar Took Three Wickets in His First 16 Overs as a Test Cricketer. He Conceded 21 Runs.
excerpt: The debutant left-arm spinner from Sri Ganganagar struck with his fourth ball in Tests and never let up. Afghanistan finished Day 2 at 113 for five, trailing India by 451.
body:
India tightened the noose on Afghanistan with a ruthless display of spin and pace bowling after declaring on 564 for eight, reducing the visitors to 113 for five at stumps on Day 2 of the one-off Test at the New PCA Stadium in New Chandigarh on Sunday.

Afghanistan trail by 451 runs with only five wickets in hand. Rahmat Shah was batting on 43 at the close, carrying the slim hope of an improbable fightback on Day 3.

## Suthar Delivers on the Biggest Stage

The afternoon belonged to Manav Suthar.

The 23-year-old left-arm spinner from Sri Ganganagar, whose father teaches at a school near the Pakistan border, had received his India cap just 24 hours earlier. On Sunday, he bowled as though he had been doing this for years.

Suthar struck with his fourth delivery in Test cricket, getting opener Abdul Malik to top-edge a sweep. Mohammed Siraj ran in from backward square leg and dived forward to take a sharp catch. The debutant was mobbed by teammates. India had their first wicket, and Suthar had his dream start.

He was not done. In a miserly spell of 15.5 overs, Suthar dismissed Rahmanullah Gurbaz — caught at second slip for 12 — and had Afsar Zazai caught and bowled for three. His figures at stumps read three for 21, an economy rate of 1.32 that underlined his control as much as his turn.

"The wicket was offering some help and my strength is getting the ball to turn," Suthar said after play. "My aim was to extract as much turn as possible because the pitch was assisting. At the same time, I wanted to keep bowling in good areas and hit the ideal length consistently. Playing for India is a dream for everyone and I am extremely happy to have received my cap."

## Krishna Adds the Pace Dimension

At the other end, Prasidh Krishna provided the speed. The tall seamer breached Sediqullah Atal's defence with a vicious delivery to claim his first Test wicket on Indian soil — a ball that moved just enough off the seam to beat the left-hander's outside edge and crash into off stump.

Krishna then broke up the most dangerous partnership of Afghanistan's innings, trapping captain Hashmatullah Shahidi leg-before for 20. The delivery nipped back sharply and caught Shahidi playing across the line.

Between them, Suthar and Krishna took five of the six wickets to fall in Afghanistan's innings — three by spin, two by pace — in a complementary attack that captain Shubman Gill orchestrated with composure.

## Saleem's Six-For in a Losing Cause

Earlier in the day, Afghanistan had their own hero in fast bowler Mohammad Saleem. The 23-year-old, who had gone wicketless in his only previous Test, completed a career-best six for 140 as India's middle and lower order fell away from the overnight score of 368 for three.

Saleem dismissed Gill for 126, caught behind off a delivery that extracted extra bounce and movement. He then knocked over Dhruv Jurel with a ball that nipped back past a lazy leave, before cleaning up Suthar (28) and Mohammed Siraj (22). He consistently bowled above 140 km/h and moved the ball both ways.

Captain Shahidi also claimed a scalp — baiting Rishabh Pant into swinging at a flighted delivery, with the batter sending the ball to long-off for 81. It was Shahidi's maiden Test wicket.

Washington Sundar held the Indian innings together at the end with a composed unbeaten 52, his sixth Test fifty, before Gill declared with the score on 564 for eight — India's fourth-fastest 500-plus total in Test history.

## The Diaspora Angle

The match at New Chandigarh represents a wider trend in Indian cricket's post-IPL transition. Eight of India's fifteen squad members had played in the IPL final just six days earlier, switching from white-ball frenzy to Test whites in under a week.

For NRI cricket fans, the emergence of Suthar is particularly noteworthy. India's spin succession — the post-Ashwin, post-Jadeja era — has been a topic of anxious conversation in diaspora cricket communities. Suthar's debut performance suggests the cupboard is not bare.

Day 3 beckons on Monday. India need five wickets. Afghanistan need a miracle.
